# 00c · `base-rules` — the extraction is the audit trail, the TOML is the rule

**Backfilled.** Generated by `MAIN_WORK/scripts/gen_base_rules.py`; the package
lives on the shelf and in no repository.

---

## What it is

A package with **no areas, no characters and no entry**, carrying only `rules/`:
ten TOML files, one per kind, **671 records**.

**⚠ `PT-1380`'s conditional was written for exactly this** — *a package that
declares areas must declare an entry; a package with no areas need not.* Both
halves of that ruling fire on this package at once: `New Game` refuses it, and
`validate` passes it.

**⚠ It is not exempt from `§4·1`.** `authors` and `summary` are required and it
carries both, like any package.

## ⚠ Why per-RECORD merge, and why flat

`PT-1386`: a campaign declaring `base-rules` and carrying its own
`rules/species.toml` is a later entry in an ordered `[requires]`, and later
entries win.

> **Merge per RECORD, not per FILE. A campaign adding one species must not have
> to restate thirty-four.**

**A record with an id already used REPLACES it. A new id ADDS. Nothing deletes** —
a campaign cannot remove a species from the game, only replace or extend, because
removal would break any other package that references it.

**⚠ And that is why subraces are flat rather than nested.** Per-record
replacement turns on `id`. A campaign adding one subrace writes **one record**;
nested under a parent it would have to restate the parent to reach it — the
per-file-versus-per-record failure `PT-1386` rejected, one level down.

**The picker filters; the file does not.** 57 records, 35 choices. Showing only
records with no parent is a **display** decision. The file's job is to hold the
rules.

## ⚠ The record shape — `PT-1389`

> **A rules record carries what the RULE says. It does not carry how we came to
> know it.**

The gap was measurable: **a class record had 30 fields and six were provenance.**
A fifth of the record was bookkeeping about where a value was read.

**Dropped:** `source` and every `*_source`, `counted_in_summary`, `phb_status`,
`table`, `state`, `kotor_reference`, `class_skills_phb`, `parent_has_own_entry`.

**Kept:** the mechanics, `availability` on a feat, `is_chain_head`, `ownable`.

**The test that settles the arguable ones:** *would a package author writing this
record BY HAND fill this field in?* They would write a vitality die. **They would
not write which line of `CLASS-ROSTER-01` it came from**, because they are not
copying from it.

> **⚠ Provenance does not vanish, it MOVES. `data/extracted/` keeps every source
> field and every fingerprint. THE JSON IS THE AUDIT TRAIL; THE TOML IS THE RULE.**
> Two records of one thing, for two different questions.

## Two decisions the rule did not cover

**A null is OMITTED, not written.** TOML has no null, and an absent field is
exactly what a hand-writing author leaves out.

**⚠ Species field labels are QUOTED, not normalised.** They are the document's
own — `"low-light_vision."` among them, and a trailing dot is a key separator in
TOML. The extraction deliberately imposes no schema on those labels (`PT-1238`:
an absent line may mean *none* or *not yet authored*), and renaming them here
would impose one through the back door.

## ⚠ What it does not settle

**Where `base-rules` lives in version control.** `§3c` says it ships with the
product and does not say from where. It cannot go in the app repo without making
Loom depend on the app — the mistake `Lens` exists to correct — and it is content
rather than code. **It is generated onto the shelf and lives in no repository.**

**Who writes a rules file.** Loom has no editor for one, and `STUDY 17` found
Aurora had none either — not one form in 105 mentions 2DA.
